source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Adivamshavatarana sub-parva. CHECKED AGAINST CE 1.61.1–102 and 1.62.1–3, 1.63.1 (GRETIL e-text of the constituted text, lab/ce; star passages and appendix lines are apparatus and were not used; Ganguli (vulgate) only as a reading aid): the king asks to hear, in order, the births among men of gods, danavas, yakshas and rakshasas (1.61.1–2: `asked`); the list of danavas born as kings: Viprachitti as Jarasandha (1.61.4), Hiranyakashipu as Shishupala (1.61.5), and on to 1.61.61 (`demons`, the two names on plaques); Drona from a portion of Brihaspati (1.61.63; plaque only); the eight Vasus born to Ganga as Shantanu's sons, by Vasishtha's curse and Indra's order, Bhishma the last of them (1.61.68–69; plaque only); Duryodhana born from a portion of Kali, hated of all the world, by whom the great feud was kindled (1.61.80–81: `kali`, the turn); his brothers, a hundred with Duhshasana first, were Paulastyas, that is rakshasas (1.61.82–83; not voiced); Yudhishthira a portion of Dharma, Bhimasena of the Wind, Arjuna of the king of the gods (1.61.84), Nakula and Sahadeva of the two Ashvins (1.61.85: `five`: the hook counts the twin Ashvins as two, so five gods); Karna, born wearing armour, a portion of the Sun (1.61.89: `karna`); of Narayana, the eternal god of gods, a portion was Vasudeva among men (1.61.90: `krishna`; the text says Vasudeva; Krishna is the same man's familiar name); Baladeva a portion of the serpent Shesha (1.61.91; not used); a portion of Shri born in Drupada's family from the middle of an altar (1.61.95: `draupadi`; the text does not name her in this verse; verse 97 calls her the one who stirs the hearts of five lords of men); whoever hears this descent of the portions, knowing origin and end, does not sink in hardships (1.61.101–102: `payoff`); Janamejaya then asks for the Kuru line from its beginning (1.62.1–2) and the answer opens on a king going to a forest with his army (1.62.3, 1.63.1: the cliffhanger). CE AGAINST THE CATALOG PLAN: the plan had "Vidura of Dharma"; in this chapter the CE reads atres tu … viduram (1.61.79: a son of Atri); Vidura is left out. ORDER: the CE's list runs danavas first, then gods; we open on the five brothers (1.61.84–85) and put Duryodhana at the turn; the source line names the chapter. Chapters 1.59–60 (the genealogies of gods and creatures) are passed over, and the source line says so. KALI here is the male spirit of the age of strife (kali), not the goddess Kali (Kālī): the plaque says so.
structure: As from episode 41 (script/ARC-41-50.md, script/ARC-51-60.md): COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words; the hook style rotates and never repeats the episode before; no episode of this batch opens on fire) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band → the episode stands alone (every name has an identifier in "names", shown as a plaque) → one question closed (loop.answeredBy), the previous one answered by 15 s (loop.prevAnsweredBy) → turn at 40–60 % after a real silence, a second silence where the story allows → one face close-up with a change of emotion → one signature shot → the cliffhanger with the source line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band that dissolves into frame 1. Per line: pal (the colour script: no hue for more than two lines), cam (≥ 4 distinct moves), tr (transitions born from the medium), amb / foley / music (three sound layers; ambLead / ambLag = J- and L-cuts). Gate: tools/gate.mjs.

names.Kali: the spirit of strife (not the goddess Kali)

loop.hookQuestion: Which five gods were the five brothers?
loop.prevQuestion: Which god was born as which hero?
loop.openQuestion: Who was the hunting king his family's story began with?

strings.recapLine: The gods were told: be born on earth, each in part.
strings.sourceLine: Adi Parva 1.61 · chapters 59–60, the genealogies, are passed over · BORI Critical Edition
strings.arcPlaylist: The whole arc is in the Vyasa Begins playlist

lines.note: COLD OPEN (a count; no fire): five warriors stand in a row on a ridge at gold dawn, dark and near; behind each, vast in the sky, a pale standing god. A pull back shows all ten. The card low.

lines.text: The king asked: which god was born as whom?
lines.say: The king asked: [p:200] which god was born as whom?
lines.note: FRAME with the unvoiced recap band (top): the teal hall: Janamejaya leans forward (plaque: Janamejaya · the king who asked); Vaishampayana opposite, empty hands opening as if to count.

lines.text: Five brothers each carried part of a god: the god of right, the wind, the king of the gods, and the twin horsemen of heaven.
lines.say: Five brothers each carried part of a god: [p:260] the god of right, [p:200] the wind, [p:200] the king of the gods, [p:200] and the twin horsemen of heaven.
lines.note: STORY 1 (messenger-dawn; answers the hook and episode 51's question): a slow track along the row; as each god is named his great figure brightens behind his man and a plaque arrives under the man: Yudhishthira · a part of Dharma; Bhima · a part of the Wind; Arjuna · a part of Indra; Nakula, Sahadeva · a part of the Ashvins. The gods are whole, large figures, never emblems.

lines.text: Karna, born in armour, was part of the sun.
lines.say: Karna, [p:100] born in armour, [p:120] was part of the sun.
lines.note: STORY 2 (wedding-turmeric): a tilt up: a lone warrior in a gold breastplate and earrings, his back to a huge low sun in which the Sun god stands in his chariot (plaque: Karna · the warrior born in armour). Small plaques, right, for two seconds each: Bhishma · last of the eight Vasus; Drona · a part of Brihaspati.

lines.text: But demons came down too. Duryodhana, who lit the great feud, was born from Kali: the spirit of strife.
lines.say: But demons came down too. [p:300] Duryodhana, [p:80] who lit the great feud, [p:120] was born from Kali: [p:160] the spirit of strife.
lines.note: STORY 3 · THE TURN (≈ 45 %) after a real silence · NEW LIGHT (venom-violet): a crowned prince with a mace, seen from below; behind him, where the others had gods, a tall dark shape with a green eye (plaques: Duryodhana · eldest of the hundred Kauravas; Kali · the spirit of strife (not the goddess Kali)). The word of the turn: STRIFE.

lines.text: Old enemies of the gods were born as mighty kings.
lines.say: Old enemies of the gods [p:100] were born as mighty kings.
lines.note: STORY 4 (wrath-crimson): a rack focus from a throne arm in the foreground to two heavy kings on thrones, each with a horned shadow thrown on the wall behind him (plaques: Jarasandha · the danava Viprachitti; Shishupala · the daitya Hiranyakashipu).

lines.text: The king heard the names of his own forefathers.
lines.say: The king heard the names [p:80] of his own forefathers.
lines.note: FRAME · THE CLOSE-UP (war-iron: the hall gone dark round him): Janamejaya's face fills the frame: wonder, then dread as he understands whose blood he carries (the brows draw, the eyes drop, then lift).

lines.text: And Narayana, god of gods? Part of him was born as Krishna.
lines.say: And Narayana, [p:100] god of gods? [p:300] Part of him [p:60] was born as Krishna.
lines.note: STORY 5 · THE SIGNATURE SHOT (pure-flame): a crane down from the great dark four-armed god in the deep blue to a dark young man below in yellow cloth with a peacock feather, standing as the god stands (plaques: Narayana · the eternal god of gods; Krishna · Vasudeva, of the Yadus).

lines.text: And a part of the goddess of fortune rose from an altar: Draupadi.
lines.say: And a part of the goddess of fortune [p:100] rose from an altar: [p:260] Draupadi.
lines.note: STORY 6 (brahma-rose): a tilt up an altar's low flame to a dark woman in a gold sari rising from its middle, a pale goddess on a lotus vast behind her (plaques: Draupadi · wife of the five brothers; Shri · the goddess of fortune).

lines.speaker: vaishampayana
lines.text: "Whoever hears this will not lose heart in hard times."
lines.say: Whoever hears this [p:150] will not lose heart [p:80] in hard times.
lines.note: THE LIT PAYOFF (a second real silence before it; ≥ 4 s with its hold; seat-ivory): the whole cast at once, lit: the five, Karna, Krishna, Draupadi and the dark prince in one long row under their gods, Vaishampayana small in front with a raised hand; a slow orbit; the hold stays on them (CE 1.61.101–102).

lines.text: The end of an arc · Vyasa Begins
lines.note: The ARC-END CARD (silent): over the lit row, a lacquer cartouche with a flame border: THE END OF AN ARC · VYASA BEGINS · Episodes 47–52 · the playlist line.

lines.text: Then the king asked for his own family's story. It began with a hunt.
lines.say: Then the king asked for his own family's story. [p:300] It began with a hunt.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (the catalog's cliffhanger, reworded to the text: 1.62.2, 1.63.1): the king's raised hand in the hall, then a green forest: a crowned rider with a bow at full gallop, deer leaping ahead, the tips of many spears behind him. The source line (top).
